module.name: docs
module.spec:
Overview: This meta-spec establishes the rules every other spec in the docs module follows. Chapter specs, concept specs, and sync specs MUST satisfy these requirements. This spec is the pedagogical authority for the documentation system.
The documentation follows outcome-based education (OBE): each chapter is designed backward from measurable learning objectives. The reader gains abilities, not just information. See glossary.spec for the formal definition of a spec and glossary.ref for the ref mechanism used throughout.
R1. Learning objectives. Every chapter spec MUST list 3-7 learning objectives. Each objective MUST use a measurable Bloom verb (identify, describe, explain, apply, analyze, evaluate, design, construct, troubleshoot). Objectives MUST NOT use unmeasurable verbs (know, understand, learn, see, grasp, appreciate).
R2. Prerequisites via ref. Every chapter spec MUST declare prerequisites via <ref> tags to concept specs and earlier chapter specs. The prereq graph MUST be acyclic: chapter N may cite chapters 1 through N-1 and any concept spec, but no chapter may cite a later chapter.
R3. Content requirements. Every chapter spec MUST enumerate what the chapter file (docs/NN-*.md) covers to satisfy the learning objectives. Content requirements use RFC 2119 keywords (MUST, SHOULD, MAY).
R4. Formative assessment. Every chapter spec MUST require at least one "Try it yourself" exercise. Exercises state a goal and a verification step, not a step-by-step recipe. Each exercise MUST be wrapped in a dedicated marker (named <shortcode>_ex) linked to the same chapter spec. Removing an exercise from a chapter file MUST produce drift on the chapter spec.
R5. Concept specs. Concept specs are atomic and MAY be cited by multiple chapter specs (spiral curriculum: a concept introduced briefly in an early chapter, defined formally in a middle chapter, applied in a later chapter). Concept specs MUST cite canonical authority (glossary.* for definitions, core.* for algorithmic contracts) via <ref>. Concept specs MUST NOT cite chapter specs. Concepts are foundational; chapters are delivery vehicles.
R6. Sync specs. Topics covered in BOTH docs/ and cli/skill.md MUST have a sync spec. The sync spec enumerates required coverage; markers in both files link to it. Changing the enumeration drifts both markers. Sync specs do NOT catch wording divergence. That requires the periodic spec audit (docs.chapter_08_spec_audit).
R7. Ref ordering. Within a chapter spec prerequisite list, concept specs MUST be cited before chapter specs. This ordering is a convention, not enforced by the scanner.
